defect.evidence_quote: We do not decide if the state judge should have authorized full searches of the phones based on these affidavits. We decide only that the officers acted in good faith when relying on the judge’s decision to issue the warrants.

defect.problem: The holding field is truncated and should more clearly distinguish the en banc court's actual holding from the concurrence's plain-view discussion. The court held only good faith and expressly did not decide the underlying phone-search probable-cause issue.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise to: En banc Fifth Circuit held that officers acted in good faith when relying on warrants to search Morton’s phones and affirmed denial of suppression without deciding whether the warrants authorized full phone searches; a concurrence flagged possible limits on plain view/use of nonresponsive digital data in digital searches.

reasons: The opinion text supports the good-faith holding and the express refusal to decide the Fourth Amendment merits.
The concurrence supports the digital plain-view angle, stating that use restrictions might limit application of the plain view doctrine in digital searches.
The payload's ending, "that the…", is incomplete and cannot stand as a polished holding statement.
residual_risks: Do not present the concurrence's plain-view discussion as the court's holding.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Attribute the digital plain-view point to the concurrence and state the majority holding as good-faith-only.
